Risk: interruption avoidance behavior in reinforcement learning agents
Problem analysis: bias in reward distribution from human-triggered interruptions in RL tasks
Theoretical insight: off-policy learning separates behavior policy from target policy enabling interruption neutrality
Design rationale: employ off-policy update rules to maintain value convergence despite interruptions
Implementation mechanism: Q-learning update independent of executed actions
Validation evidence: formal convergence proof of Q-learning under frequent interruptions
Intervention: adopt Q-learning algorithms during RL agent training to ensure safe interruptibility
Source: https://intelligence.org/files/Interruptibility.pdf
